page: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 7443P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated system features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.85 GHz, supported by hyper-threading. The memory configuration consists of 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing 5.33 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong computational capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 10%, and strong multi-core performance in the top 25%. PassMark testing confirms these results, with the CPU score and database operations both ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly efficient, with PassMark memory scores placing in the top 10%, though memory bandwidth for large block read and write operations remains in the middle 50% range. For language model workloads, the system delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 388.22 tokens per second on small 135M models and strong performance of 29.13 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare metal architecture provides dedicated hardware resources without virtualization overhead, offering high resource density and predictable performance for demanding workloads. The combination of 48 vCPUs, 256 GB of RAM, and local SSD storage makes this server well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
